conviction_note: abs_move 9.5 (event-implied 9.92, own median 7.64, last two prints -7.6/-7.9, Q3 2025 -12.2 on an EPS beat with a comp miss) times a lean of p_up 47. Evidence is mixed: a record-warm September and fourth-warmest October on an outerwear-led quarter, plus peer fuel and freight costs into Q4, against TJX's Marmaxx strengthening late in the quarter, an easy compare and a lowered EPS bar. The findings sum to -0.9 and the scaled number is -0.57; both are small because the evidence offsets and the downside the evidence points to is already where the skew (+6 vol points of puts) and a 21% drop since the last print sit.

positioning_check: Short interest 3.34M shares, 5.35% of float, 3.45 days to cover (Fintel/NYSE, latest settlement shown 2026-10-15, https://fintel.io/ss/us/burl); Sep 30 settlement 3.21M, 1.9 DTC per massive.com. Not crowded, so a squeeze is not a strong mechanism. Skew +5.98 vol points (puts bid), put/call OI 0.56, ATM IV 114%. Stock $238.32, -36% from 52w high, +4.9% off 52w low, about -21% since the Aug 27 print, below the 200-day (~$305). Zacks Rank #5, with FY estimates cut 5.5% in 60 days. findings.finding: September 2026 was the warmest September on record for the contiguous US (NOAA, reported 2026-10-08) and October 2026 the fourth-warmest October, with the Ohio Valley third-warmest. That is the window management called 'a very important driver of our comp, especially in Q3' on the Aug 27 call, while adding that it 'deliberately planned down our outerwear businesses'. Net: Q3 comp is more likely in the bottom half of the 1-3% guide than above the ~2%+ the street usually carries.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-25): comp +1% against a 2.4% sell-side average, with management blaming mild Sep/Oct weather. The stock fell 12.24% despite a 13% EPS beat. Q2 2026: comp 2% and a revenue miss, -7.64%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down ~21% since the print and puts are bid. What would differ if fully priced: consensus revenue would sit at the guide midpoint ($2.98B), not the top ($3.00B). It has not moved there, while EPS estimates were cut.
findings.independence: TJX (2026-11-18) said 'unseasonably warm weather in the U.S. and Canada has been holding back consumer demand in some categories' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm); Climate Central October 2026 briefing, fourth-warmest October (https://www.climatecentral.org/climate-briefings/october-2026); Canada Goose said October comps stayed negative on warm weather (https://retail-insider.com/?p=211165). Mitigant from BURL's own call: outerwear planned down (https://www.webull.com/news/15497683394880512). This is a weather-to-company transmission, i.e. a proxy, though one the company itself named.

findings.finding: On the Aug 27 call the CFO said the Q3-to-date comp trend was 'within our 1% to 3% Q3 comp guidance range', with August 'our toughest monthly compare in the third quarter' and compares easing in September and October. The prior-year Q3 comp was only +1%, itself held back by mild weather, so the two-year stack is undemanding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BURL has held its comp guide recently (Q2: 2% inside its range) but sold off on comp prints near the low end. An in-range comp has not been rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: this is in the wire from the call. Small residual because the easy Sep/Oct compare offsets part of the weather headwind in finding 1; previews dwell on stalled traffic, not on the compare.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comp +1% (https://finviz.com/news/238694/burlington-stores-burl-reports-q3-earnings-what-key-metrics-have-to-say). Shares the call document with finding 1's mitigant.

findings.finding: TJX (Nov 18, after BURL last spoke): Marmaxx comp +2% on flat transactions, with comps that 'strengthened in the second half of the quarter' (i.e. October). It expects further Marmaxx improvement in Q4 and 'sales momentum to accelerate throughout the holiday season'. TJX stock rose ~6% on the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No BURL-specific history on peer read-throughs found. BURL's own prints have been sold 3 of the last 4.
findings.why_not_priced: BURL's 5-day run-up is only +1.34%, so the off-price late-quarter improvement TJX reported has not lifted BURL. If priced, BURL would have tracked TJX's +6% day.
findings.independence: Placer.ai (2026-11-16): T.J. Maxx overall and same-store visits turned positive in September and growth accelerated in October (https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/off-price-on-course-ross-and-tjx-in-q3-2026); TJX +6.08% on the print (https://finviz.com/news/424720/tjx-shares-jump-608-as-third-quarter-revenue-beats-estimates-and-fy2027-outlook-strengthens). Peer evidence; no BURL-specific traffic series was found.

findings.finding: Ross (Nov 19): Q3 comp +8% on a 7% compare, 'mainly' traffic-driven, Placer.ai same-store visits +12.3%. Value-end demand is healthy but concentrated at Ross, while BURL's last disclosed per-location traffic was negative (Placer Q1 2026 -2.1%; Q2 comp transactions flat). Ross's lead reinforces the share-shift bear case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BURL sold off on traffic and comp disappointment at Q3 2025 (-12.2%) and Q2 2026 (-7.6%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the share-loss narrative is in downgrade chatter (Nov 13) and the stock is near its lows. Residual: the size of Ross's traffic lead in the same quarter is new since BURL spoke. The sign is ambiguous, because a strong value consumer also helps BURL.
findings.independence: Placer.ai Q3 2026 (https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/off-price-on-course-ross-and-tjx-in-q3-2026); Placer.ai Q1 2026 BURL per-location -2.1% (https://placer.ai/anchor/articles/off-price-picks-up-even-more-steam-in-q1-2026---led-by-ross). Peer proxy, not a BURL number.

findings.finding: The EPS bar is beatable: consensus $1.69 sits at the top of a $1.60-1.70 guide and the whisper is $1.81. FY estimates were cut 5.5% in 60 days (Zacks, 10-29). BURL beat its operating-margin guide by 'well above the high end' in Q2 (+100bp ex refunds) and beat Q3 2025 EPS by 13%. An EPS beat is the likely print, but this stock has sold its EPS beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: EPS beat 13%, stock -12.24% on comps. Q2 2026: EPS beat, -7.64% on revenue and guide. EPS beats are not paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper at $1.81 already sits above the guide, so an EPS beat is expected. The residual is that FY estimates fell while the company has not cut, so a held or raised FY guide reads as a relief.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/423368/burlingtons-q3-tests-whether-tariff-refund-reinvestment-can-revive-stalled-traffic, 2026-11-16); Q2 call margin beat (https://www.webull.com/news/15497683394880512).

findings.finding: Q4/FY guide risk from peer costs: TJX said 'higher freight and fuel costs pressured Q3 gross margin' and its Q4 outlook 'assumes additional fuel costs'. Ross trimmed Q4 EPS by $0.01 at each end while holding comps. BURL's Q4 is guided at comp +1-3% and EPS $5.05-5.15, absorbing ~60% of the $55M refund reinvestment, with FY consensus $11.92 near the top of $11.77-11.97. A warm November start adds risk to an outerwear-heavy Q4, so the FY may be held only by trimming Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the Q3 guide came in below the street ($1.60-1.70 vs ~$2.03), -7.64%. Q3 2025: cautious guide, -12.24%. Guidance has been the line that moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus FY $11.92 still sits near the top of the guide. If fuel and freight plus a warm November were priced, FY consensus would sit at or below the guide midpoint ($11.87).
findings.independence: Ross Q4 EPS trimmed and fuel costs flagged as a risk (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000745732/000074573226000047/q326exhibit991.htm). Shares the TJX release with findings 1 and 3, but this is a different line (costs, Q4).

findings.finding: Cannibalization from new stores rose to ~1.5 points of comp in Q2 (vs ~1 point historically) and management expects it to persist through the year, after a record 149 net new stores in 12 months. The headwind is structural but already in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raised as a concern on the Q2 call, which sold -7.64%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the company's guide and in previews, so nearly priced. Residual only if the company raises the cannibalization estimate.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview cites the same figure (https://finviz.com/news/423368/burlingtons-q3-tests-whether-tariff-refund-reinvestment-can-revive-stalled-traffic). Same underlying call.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly negative, which agrees with the +6-point put skew and the 21% drop since the last print. That suggests the downside is largely priced, which is why p_up sits at 47 rather than lower, and the late-quarter peer improvement (TJX, the easy compare) is the part the price has not reflected.
lessons_applied: Weather finding cut -1.5 to -1.0: lesson 5 and 'what has worked' (reasoning from weather has not paid; it is a proxy), partly offset because the company and TJX both named the effect.
Ross share-shift cut -0.5 to -0.3: lesson 5, a peer proxy with no BURL number behind it; the sign is ambiguous.
EPS-beat finding cut +0.8 to +0.4: lesson 1, this name sold EPS beats at -12.2% (Q3 2025) and -7.6% (Q2 2026).
Unverified downgrade cut -0.2 to -0.1: lesson 6/3, unnamed firm, AI-generated page whose own list contradicts it.
p_up 46 to 47: lesson 7, my lean agrees with a +6 put skew, so the downside is likely priced.
Left standing: TJX peer read (+0.8) and the guide/fuel-cost finding (-1.0), both peer primary documents dated after BURL last spoke ('what has worked').
